franchisor_revenue_streams.initial_franchise_fee: Upfront fee for franchise rights, training, site selection, opening assistance
franchisor_revenue_streams.continuing_franchise_fees: Ongoing royalties (typically % of franchisee sales) for brand use, support, advertising
franchisor_revenue_streams.equipment_sales: Sale of equipment, inventory to franchisee (if applicable)

initial_franchise_fee_accounting.performance_obligations: Identify distinct performance obligations (franchise license, training, site selection, etc.)
initial_franchise_fee_accounting.revenue_recognition: Recognize as each performance obligation satisfied

typical_pattern.pre_opening_services: Training, site selection → Over time or point in time as services provided
typical_pattern.franchise_license: Right to use (if no ongoing support beyond continuing fees) → Point in time when franchise opens. Right to access (if significant ongoing involvement) → Over time.

continuing_franchise_fees.revenue_recognition: Recognize as franchisee makes sales (royalty exception under ASC 606)
continuing_franchise_fees.accounting: DR AR, CR Royalty Revenue (as franchisee reports sales)

refund_provisions.if_refundable: May need to defer recognition if significant refund risk (variable consideration constraint)
refund_provisions.substantial_services: If franchisor has substantial remaining services, defer initial fee until services substantially performed

area_franchise_agreements.definition: Franchisee granted rights to open multiple locations in territory
area_franchise_agreements.accounting: Initial fee allocated to: (1) Services for first franchise, (2) Option to open additional franchises (if material)
area_franchise_agreements.options: Evaluate if option for additional franchises provides material right (would require allocation)

example_initial_fee.facts: Franchisor charges $50K initial fee. Includes: License $30K (allocated), training $15K (allocated), opening assistance $5K (allocated). Franchise opens June 1.
example_initial_fee.performance_obligations: 1. Training (completed May 1), 2. Opening assistance (completed May 30), 3. License (ready June 1)

revenue_recognition.may_30: DR AR $5K, CR Revenue $5K (opening assistance completed)
revenue_recognition.june_1: DR AR $30K, CR Revenue $30K (license available, franchise opens - assuming right to use)

example_continuing_fees.facts: Franchisee reports $200K sales in Month 1. Royalty rate 6%.
example_continuing_fees.accounting: Royalty = $200K × 6% = $12K. DR AR $12K, CR Royalty Revenue $12K

equipment_and_inventory_sales.treatment: Separate performance obligations (distinct from franchise rights)
equipment_and_inventory_sales.revenue_recognition: When control transfers (typically point in time)
equipment_and_inventory_sales.pricing: Should reflect standalone selling price (not bundled with franchise fee)

repurchase_options.if_franchisor_option: May indicate lease rather than sale (if repurchase at less than FV)
repurchase_options.if_franchisee_option: Evaluate if affects revenue recognition (typically doesn't defer initial fee)

bargain_purchases.if_required_purchases: If franchisee must purchase from franchisor at above-market prices, may indicate initial fee should be adjusted

cpa_exam_tips: Initial franchise fee: Allocate to performance obligations, recognize as satisfied
Continuing fees: Recognize as franchisee makes sales (sales-based royalty)
Franchise license: Right to use (point in time when opens) or right to access (over time if ongoing support)
Pre-opening services: Recognize as performed (training, assistance)
Refundable fees: May need to defer if significant refund risk

revenue_recognition_approach: 1. Identify performance obligations (license, training, assistance, etc.)
2. Allocate transaction price (initial fee) to each obligation
3. Recognize revenue as each obligation satisfied
4. Continuing fees: Recognize as franchisee sales occur
common_mistakes: Recognizing entire initial fee upfront (should allocate to obligations)
Recognizing continuing fees upfront (should recognize as franchisee sales occur)
Not evaluating if license is right to use vs right to access
Forgetting to consider refund provisions (variable consideration)

key_points: Initial franchise fee: Allocate to performance obligations, recognize as satisfied
Continuing fees: Sales-based royalties, recognize as franchisee makes sales
Franchise license: Right to use (point in time) or right to access (over time)
Refundable fees: Consider variable consideration constraint
